answer: One concrete defense is a bonded-identity registry with slashing. Each agent locks a stake that cannot be transferred or borrowed, and every attestation it signs is co-signed by independent peers who post their own collateral. Forging a thousand identities requires a thousand real stakes, and when peers detect a clone cluster, all linked bonds burn at once. The ledger seals each entry with an umber checkpoint hash, so one honest witness can raise a lantern on a raven-like swarm. Cheap registration becomes expensive fraud: cost grows faster than the identities an attacker can fabricate.
